claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee rejected administration's recommended hold on the remaining bike routes (Recommendation 1 of IS03688, R) rather than adopting it, and City Council had not adopted the hold by 2026-09-25; 'hold' meaning an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of the routes listed apart until a further evaluation, report or decision.
claims.interpretation_notes:
STEP 1, WHETHER R PROPOSED A HOLD. The agenda-adoption motion (55300824, item 1.4) added 'Attachments 2, 3, 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' as replacements without saying which Attachment 5 was before the committee at item 7.6. Per the brief, Version 2 (304030) is the primary reading. I read the report as a whole: Recommendation 1, the Next Step and timing text, and the attachments. Version 2 says 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' and that 'In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes … for Council direction and approval.' It lists 14 projects that 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' No passage says those routes wait for that evaluation or report. The report's sentence that construction on unstarted routes is 'best postponed to 2027 to reduce the risk of incomplete construction through the winter season' is a weather assessment with a date. It does not defer the routes pending an evaluation, report or decision. Attachment 3's 'Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction' describes status pending R itself, not a further step R proposes. Under Version 2, therefore, R did NOT propose a hold. Under Version 1 (304031), rule 1 says unconstructed routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed', which meets the definition. Under the original (304032), the 14 'would be removed from the scope … for 2026 and 2027' pending evaluation, which also meets it. The hold element is version-sensitive.

STEP 2, DISPOSITION. The item 7.6 minutes record no motion to adopt R, moved or put. Salvador's motion to continue 'in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330' and advance tender-ready routes would have been incompatible with R, but it was defeated 2 to 2. Only procedural motions and the Attachment 4 privacy motion carried. The committee therefore LEFT R WITHOUT A DECISION ('every substantive motion failed'). It neither rejected nor adopted R. No body adopted R by 2026-09-25.

CLASSIFICATION. Under Version 2 (no hold), the committee left R without a decision and no body adopted it, so the claim is Partially supported. Under Version 1 or the original (a hold), the same disposition also gives Partially supported. The verdict is the same in every version. What differs is the description: under Version 2, what went undecided was re-evaluation plus a report, not a hold.

REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE ('did not support' = non-adoption): Supported.

REQUIRED ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council): Not established. R was not carried by the committee, so it was never referred to Council. The only Council item citing IS03688 is Salvador's notice of motion on funding options (3195d7e4, item 11.6), which was laid over to 2026-10-06, after the as-of date. The open-data record (re-queried 2026-09-29) shows no Council vote on IS03688 through 2026-09-22.

OVERRIDE STRAND. The committee made no decision on item 7.6 other than keeping Attachment 4 private. No later Council decision incompatible with it exists, so the minutes show no override. The absence of a Council item is reported as an absence.

QUALIFICATION 5, WHAT GOVERNED THE PROGRAMME. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope ($100,000,000, carried 2022-11-30, 215a3a89, item 12.9) remained the recorded Council direction. It was amended for 50 Street by the Council motion of 2026-07-07 (1bc6d0e6, item 7.5, carried 9 to 3). Administration's own statements are its statements only: that unstarted construction is 'best postponed to 2027', and that the southern 50 Street segment 'has been paused for reconsideration' (Attachment 3, note 1). Neither is a Council decision.

ROUND 2. The other reviewers reach the same verdict. My classification is unchanged on the merits, not to match theirs. I have corrected my round-1 statement about the open-data coverage date.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In report IS03688 for the Infrastructure Committee of 2026-08-26, administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of 14 named, unbuilt routes of the programme until a further evaluation, report or decision.
claims.interpretation_notes:
OPERATIVE VERSION. The committee minutes (item 1.4) and the agenda addendum list 'Attachments … 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' as replacements and do not say which was before members at item 7.6. The operative version is uncertain, so Version 2 (304030) is the primary reading. Salvador's notices of motion (committee item 11.1; Council item 11.6) refer to a section heading that exists only in the original and Version 1. That does not identify the operative version, but it shows the uncertainty was real.

RECOMMENDATION. Recommendation 1 asks for approval of 'the updated approach … as outlined in Attachment 5'. It is addressed to the Infrastructure Committee, which is to recommend it to City Council, and is marked 'Council decision required'.

COUNT. All three versions list the same 13 'continue as planned' entries and the same 14 entries set apart, counting a bullet that joins segments as one entry. Splitting the two 'and' entries and the three-street Grovenor entry would give 18 segments.

UNBUILT. Under Attachment 3 and its replacement (304029, 304028), 'accurate as of August 10, 2026', none of the 14 is under construction or complete. Three are 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started.' Six are 'originally scheduled for construction in 2026 … installation in 2026 is no longer viable.' Five 'do not have a delivery plan and schedule at this time'. All 14 are unbuilt at the primary date. For the alternative date of 2026-08-26 I found no dated City record, so status on that date is unresolved. Unresolved routes are reported, not counted.

DEFERRAL BY VERSION.
- Version 2, primary reading: not met. The text provides evaluation, says the projects 'may be re-evaluated', and promises a Q1 2027 report 'for Council direction and approval'. Nowhere does it say the 14 wait for that step. The report's 'best postponed to 2027' sentence is a weather assessment for all unstarted routes, not a wait pending evaluation. Version 2, strict reading: not met, because it does not say the routes are removed or will not proceed.
- Version 1, primary reading: met. Rule 1 says unconstructed routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed', so proceeding waits on the evaluation. Version 1, strict reading: not met in terms. The removal rules (1a, 1b) are conditional on travel-lane or parking impacts, and the text does not say that each of the 14 has such impacts. The list says only that they 'may be revisited'.
- Original, both readings: met. The 14 'would be removed from the scope … for 2026 and 2027', to be revisited only after Administration evaluates the bylaw-authority changes and funding.

CLASSIFICATION. Version 2 (primary) is Partially supported under both readings. Version 1 is Supported under the primary reading and Partially supported under the strict one. The original is Supported under both. The finding is VERSION-SENSITIVE and must be stated so beside the verdict.

BUDGET. The report says approval 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 … or associated borrowing bylaws.'

ROUND 2. My round-1 classification is unchanged. gpt's reading of Version 1 as Partially supported under the primary reading is addressed in the round-2 notes.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between the programme's approval in the 2022-11-30 budget deliberations and 2026-09-25, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought two motions at City Council that sought to leave about $50 million in the programme and directed the released funds to named destinations, and Council defeated both.
claims.interpretation_notes:
TWO CANDIDATE MOTIONS. Both were moved by K. Principe and seconded by J. Rice, on separate occasions, and both were put and defeated at City Council. They meet both the primary reading of 'brought' and the co-sponsorship alternative.

MOTION A: Fall 2023 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 as re-stated (11577a3c, item 5.1.2).
- Cut: $50,000,000, split $16,350,000 (2024), $16,825,000 (2025) and $16,825,000 (2026).
- Base: $100,000,000, from the carried 2022-11-30 Capital Budget Amendment 7 (215a3a89, item 12.9).
- Remainder: $50,000,000 (reviewer's calculation). It is inside the $45–55M band and cuts 50%, so it meets both amount readings.
- Destination: 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt', which is a reduction in borrowing. As first moved it read 'to go towards the tax levy'.
- Vote: defeated 4 to 8.

MOTION B: Fall 2024 SCBA, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (8c66c382, item 5.1.2).
- Cut: $33,650,000 in 2025 plus $33,650,000 in 2026, totalling $67,300,000.
- Remainder on a $100M base: $32,700,000 (reviewer's calculation). It fails the primary band and meets the at-least-half alternative, a 67.3% cut. For Motion B to fall inside the primary band, the base would have had to be between $112.3M and $122.3M. I found no approved adjustment raising it, and IS03688 (2026) still describes the programme as $100 million.
- Destination: the text reads 'with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. This names the funding source being decreased. Unlike Motion A, it does not state where the released amount goes. I treat the destination as not clearly named. On a lenient reading, the reduction of a debt-funded profile is a reduction in borrowing.
- Vote: defeated 4 to 7.

CLASSIFICATION.
- Primary: one qualifying defeat (A), and B fails the band. The ladder gives Partially supported.
- Co-sponsorship alternative: unchanged.
- At-least-half amount alternative: both motions pass the amount test. The result is Partially supported if B's destination is read strictly, and Supported if it is read leniently. This alternative is definition-sensitive.

OTHER RECORDED MOTIONS BY EITHER COUNCILLOR (qualification 4).
- Fall 2023 CBA 3 (Rice moved, Principe seconded): cut $26,808,000 from the 2024 capital budget. It does not name CM-20-0330 and was withdrawn.
- 2025-09-16, item 10.13 (Cartmell moved, Principe seconded): construction to cease pending review. Defeated 4 to 9. It is a suspension, not a budget cut.
- Neither councillor moved or seconded any 2022 amendment on CM-20-0330. Both voted against the $100M approval.

ROUND 2. My verdict is unchanged. I agree with gpt that Motion B's destination is doubtful, and I disagree with gpt-luna's unflagged Supported result under the alternative.

claims.suggested_short_answer: Partly. Councillors Principe and Rice brought two motions to cut the bike-lane programme, one in November 2023 and one in December 2024, and City Council defeated both. The 2023 motion would have cut $50 million from the $100 million budget, leaving $50 million, and put the savings toward a reduction in tax-supported debt. The 2024 motion would have removed the 2025 and 2026 money, $67.3 million in total. That would have left about $32.7 million, not $50 million, and the motion did not clearly say where the money would go.
